answer: The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce. Each submission hangs on the hollow of a task receipt, and the river is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. The design leans on cost-of-replication accounting, published publicly on failure, no identity may audit its own recruit. Written in a verbs first, step by step register, it stays short. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the crystal of payment, so volume alone buys nothing.
